highest_value_fixes: 1. SCENE FIX: Restore architectural continuity. In A's nave remove or correctly assemble the floating wooden blocks; in both arms close the blue upper-corner gaps visible at night and give the upper ledges/roof strips legible supports. B is the stronger nave starting point, but needs purposeful reception, waiting and portal zones rather than more uniform scatter.

2. SCENE FIX: Rebuild night value structure and character contact. Reduce the uniform beige veil, keep cool shadow mass, place warm light around visible fixtures, retain far-room depth, and establish boot/furniture contact shadows. Recheck shrine base stippling and shiny wall artifacts. Day/rain needs a legible window-light/weather distinction appropriate to an interior.

3. NEEDS NEW OR SUBSTANTIALLY REWORKED ART: Distinct Hall portal surrounds, readable biome emblems and purpose-designed shrine pedestals would address the generic door/lectern identity. Use coherent structural profiles and calmer large material shapes rather than dense brown edge noise. Existing trainer silhouette is serviceable; these rear static frames do not justify a new humanoid mesh or certify its face/animation.
bar_a_world_fit_rationale: NO for A; NO for B at the requested completed-presentation bar. Brown timber, pale stone/plaster and teal cloth are directionally compatible with the Meadows palette, and the trainer's blue/cream outfit and backpack communicate an adventurer. B is more coherent because its nave lacks the floating blocks. Neither arm yet has the key art's authored silhouette hierarchy, inhabited warmth, grounded character or convincing spatial depth. This judges palette, mood and shape intent, not painted pixel fidelity. Human door/bench scale is broadly plausible relative to the disclosed 1.80 m trainer; the vast repetitive hall and weak contact cues make the whole less convincing. All 26 A/B pairs were viewed full-size, with the contact sheet used for small-size readability. High and Medium show the same material visual deficits at this scoring precision. Isolated interior only: no claim about exterior, traversal or full-world acceptance.
bar_b_atmosphere_rationale: NO for A; NO for B: these frames do not yet present as the same commercial visual class/kind of game as the supplied Palworld imagery with Valheim-class atmosphere. The stylized third-person adventurer and medieval hub are genre-compatible, but plain repetitive architecture, disconnected geometry in A, weak grounding, nearly uniform day light and beige night wash read as a prototype environment. B wins nave clarity, not shipping finish; shrine pairs are effectively equal at the judged scale. The Palworld references retain strong grounded subjects, clear light direction and layered contrast even at small size. Absence of creatures in this scoped Hall diagnostic is not itself scored as a defect. Still images supply no performance, traversal or animation evidence.
